# 08-fresco — sources

Back-test entry `08-fresco.yaml`: Fresco, the AI scribe for construction superintendents (YC Fall 2024).
Written 2026-10-22 from public material only. Quotes are verbatim from the page named; "Author's choice" marks the
smallest plausible choice made where the public material is silent.

Main sources:
- [HN] Launch HN: Fresco (YC F24), 2024-11-21 — https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=42204939
- [LYC] Launch YC: Fresco, the scribe for construction, 2024-10-23 — https://www.ycombinator.com/launches/M73-fresco-the-scribe-for-construction
- [YCP] YC company page — https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/fresco (now "AI-powered takeoff and estimating for Division 8 construction")
- [KOE] A contractor's daily-log expectations on Procore's support site — https://support.procore.com/tc/Koester/Site_Map/Koester_Expectations_-_Daily_Logs
- [SWI] Swiftask, Procore daily reports page (vendor) — https://swiftask.ai/ai-integration/procore/intelligent-daily-reports
- [BLS] BLS Occupational Outlook, construction managers — https://www.bls.gov/ooh/management/construction-managers.htm
- [OPU] Launch HN: Opusense (field reports for site inspectors), 2025-05-20 — https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=44042791

## The eight founder-emulation items

1. **Who.** Construction superintendents on commercial jobs.
   [HN] "Superintendents are the busiest and most expensive people on construction sites."
   [LYC] "That’s the reality for 210k+ construction superintendents (or supervisors, foremen, PMs, etc.) across the USA."
   → `roles[superintendent]`, `context.actor`, `actor_plural`. Author's choice: "on commercial jobs" (the founders ask
   for introductions to commercial general contractors in [LYC]).

2. **What (the job).** Keep the record of the day's work, for liability and disputes.
   [HN] "30-200 photos per day to document site progress (mostly for liability reasons, or in case of a dispute with the
   owner over delays and deliverables)"; photos used to create "daily logs", "structured documents that account for the
   work done on site on any given day". [KOE] the log is "a critical piece of documentation in the arbitration of a
   dispute". → `statements.problem`, `context.job`, `interpretations.problem`.

3. **When / where.** At the end of the day, after the site walks, in the trailer.
   [HN] "At the end of the day, they'll spend a few hours uploading those photos into OneDrive, or project management
   software like Procore or ACC." [YCP] "We were curious what superintendents were doing for hours in their trailers at
   the end of the day." [LYC] "supes are spending up to 3 hours a day creating documents". → `context.circumstance`, `occasion: daily log`.
   Author's choice: the recall window {5, WORKING_DAYS} and Frequency 4 to 5 working days out of 5 (the posts say "per
   day"; a five-day site week is assumed). Prevalence `p_80_100` ("Nearly all") follows from the same "per day".

4. **Which people (the comparable group).** Superintendents at US general contractors whose jobs run on Procore or ACC.
   [LYC] "210k+ construction superintendents ... across the USA"; "Project management tools like Procore and ACC have
   dramatically increased documentation requirements". [YCP] "driving to Napa, South Bay, and around SF". → `context.segment`,
   `market: US`.

5. **Who pays.** The general contractor, per site.
   [HN] "we charge per site per month, which includes unlimited users on any given construction project".
   → `persona.decision_maker: {role: contractor}`, the BUYER role. Author's choice: the decider is the contractor's
   "operations lead" and the role to test is "The CFO" (a second role, "The project executive", listed); Purchase
   friction's three steps ("A trial on one live job" tested, a Procore check, a security review) and Commitment's step
   "start a paid pilot on one site" are the author's. Public material names no buyer title; [LYC] asks for
   introductions to general contractors by firm, not by role.

6. **Mechanism.** Narrated short videos turned into notes, texted to the crew, pushed to Procore/ACC.
   [HN] "Supers simply take short videos with voiceover, or upload photos, and Fresco does the rest, creating notes with
   transcription, photos, assignees, and due dates. Supers can easily text their crew action items, and receive texts
   back". "We also route this to whatever project management software they're using with a single click."
   [LYC] the narrated example "The beam in the southwest corner of room 134 is corroded and needs replacement by Alex.";
   "Supes who use Fresco complete their notes, on average, 90% faster."
   → `statements.solution`, `solution_mechanism`, Compatibility and Adoption friction items. Relative advantage's two
   benefits are from [HN] ("during their site walks, not after") and [LYC] ("90% faster"); their wording is the author's.

7. **Price.** About $1k per site per month, less with multi-site or multi-month terms.
   [HN] "The typical price is $1k/month, but we offer discounts for multi-month or multi-site commitments."
   → `commercial.price` {800, 1000, month}. Author's choice: the low end of $800 stands for the stated discounts.
   Existing sacrifice: 30 to 60 hours a month per site at an hourly rate of 55 — from [LYC] "up to 3 hours a day" and
   [HN] "a few hours uploading", taken as 1.5 to 3 hours on about twenty working days (author's arithmetic). The rate is
   [BLS] "$55.28 per hour" (median, construction managers, May 2025), the author's stand-in: no superintendent wage is
   in the public material. Ability to pay is derived by code (24% to 61%).

8. **Occasions.** The narrated beam; a school refit report; the uploads and logs at the end of the day.
   [LYC] on a school refit walkthrough: "Normally, creating the final report takes 2+ hours."
   [HN] "few supers have time to do this thoroughly, so these photos aren't very searchable." No named customer quote
   exists in public; the occasions below are scripted from these and from practitioner comments.

No respondent carries the name of a commenter, customer or founder.

## Open
- The verdict was scripted to be plausible and not obviously "build": the problem holds on how often but people
  disagree on whether the log is one of their two worst difficulties; the solution splits on the benefit and on
  talking over videos on site; the price fails (two of eight at the founder's band or above) while the cost it would
  replace is above the price. This is the author's reading of the thread's sceptics, not a measured result.
- No public account names a buyer title at a general contractor; the decider, the tested role "The CFO", the purchase
  steps and the Commitment step are the author's.
- hourly_rate 55 is a proxy (construction managers, not superintendents).
- Existing sacrifice picks use `period: quarter` (the corpus's convention), although the registry's recall period for a
  monthly cost reads "last month"; the values are the monthly figures times three.
- The window {5, WORKING_DAYS} is the author's; the public posts say "per day".

founder.order_why: The run from context to problem to solution is how I'd explain Fresco, but Offer a pilot comes before anything has been asked about price or who pays, so I'm deciding on a pilot without the commercial terms it depends on.
founder.asked_twice: Screens 3 and 5 carry the same question, 'Before we test anything, let's define exactly where this idea applies', with the recency question between them.
founder.missing: Nothing asks who pays or what it costs: the general contractor buys, per site, at about $1k a month with multi-site or multi-month discounts, and the person using it (the superintendent) is not the person paying. There is also no question on the time it replaces (up to 3 hours a day), which is what the price has to be judged against.

PRIMARY.order_why: It goes from whether I'm on Procore or ACC and retyped notes recently, to the idea, then whether talking on site is workable, whether it would have helped, and whether I'd actually do it, which is a sensible flow.
PRIMARY.missing: It never asked how I handle the daily log today, like how long it takes me or when I get to it, or whether the output would hold up in a dispute with an owner over delays.

screens.why2: "Pilot" is plain to me, since it is how I'd sell a job-site trial, but "people who say yes get a line" is circular because the line is itself the yes-or-no ask, so I read it twice.
screens.why3: Whether I want names for a trial is my own call at launch, when I am actively looking for sites to run Fresco on.
screens.why4: Yes and No are the only two choices, they are distinct and plainly worded, and no escape is needed for a decision that is mine.
screens.why5: I picked Yes and the screen keeps that without rewriting anything of mine, and the generic wording does not contradict my one-site pilot.
screens.instead: Offer a pilot? At the end of the study we ask everyone: "Would you try this for real? Leave your email." You see who left one on the Pilot tab. Options: Yes, ask them / No pilot

screens.why1: Just before the study goes out, it makes sense to settle who will put the questions to my superintendents, and the screen follows naturally from the pilot offer.
screens.why2: The question is plain, but the hint packs in video, typing, voice, recording, credits and text delivery, and it says 'face' nowhere while speaking only of voices, so I need a second read to know what I am picking.
screens.why3: I can choose an interviewer by listening to two short samples and deciding which would sound right to a super, with no knowledge needed beyond my own taste and my customers.
screens.why4: Two named interviewers with a five-second sample each are complete and distinct for this choice, the preselected one is clear, and an escape chip is not needed when the default stands.
screens.why5: It keeps my 'construction superintendents' and the text-message link, and nothing it says changes what I typed about Fresco.
screens.instead: Who should ask construction superintendents your questions? Daphne is picked for you; tap Saskia to hear her and switch. It costs 400 credits either way, and people can talk, type or tap.

screens.why1: Right after choosing who asks the questions and just before sending, it is obvious why I am now picking how my superintendents will answer.
screens.why2: The three choices are easy to follow, but "She catches every spoken answer in a quiet room, and more than 9 in 10 where it is loud" and the status lines "Still recording" and "Ready when Daphne is" take a second read.
screens.why3: I know how supers work, on noisy sites or in the trailer and mostly on their phones, so I can judge which format they would actually finish.
screens.why4: The three options are complete and distinct, but only Read and tap is ready now, and the option titled Let them choose says "Daphne or text" while the option it refers to is called "Read and tap".
screens.why5: My pick of Read and tap is kept as typed, and nothing here changes what my study or product means.
screens.instead: How should construction superintendents answer? AI interviewer: Daphne asks each question aloud and it is written on screen, and she may miss some spoken answers on a loud site (ready in a few minutes). Read and tap: they read each question and tap or type (ready now). Let them choose: they pick Daphne or Read and tap when they open the link (ready in a few minutes).

screens.why1: Having chosen how superintendents will answer, the next obvious step before sending is deciding who gets the link.
screens.why2: The choice is clear on first read, but "Contacts page" assumes I know a part of Keel I have not been through in this flow, and "Who gets a link?" reads a little oddly under a kicker that says the interviews are already sent.
screens.why3: I know how I reach supers, through the people I have met driving to sites and through contractor introductions, so I can answer this from what I actually do.
screens.why4: The three routes are distinct and cover how I would reach people, but the option text "From a search on the Contacts page" is Keel's own wording, not mine, and needs explaining.
screens.why5: My pick of people I know by name, each with their own link, is kept exactly as I meant it.
screens.instead: Who gets a link? People I know by name (I send each one their own link) / People I find with Keel (search for people here, Keel makes a link for each, and I send them) / A group, with one open link (I post one link where they already are; each person signs in with Google, then is interviewed)

screens.why_b1: The verdict "Too few to call" is stated at the top, and "4 answered · 5 needed to call it" sits beside it on every card, so I know no belief has been decided and why.
screens.why_b2: The stage page draws no chart, but the tally and the bar of 5 are plain; it takes a second look to work out why 7 people answered when each card says 4, and the screen doesn't explain the gap.
screens.why_b3: Compatibility, Relative advantage and Adoption friction carry the same names and belief lines I checked on the way in.
screens.why_b4: "5 needed to call it" implies I need at least one more counted answer per belief, but the screen never tells me to get more answers, who to ask, or what this means for building the scribe.
screens.why_b5: It makes no claim about my solution from 4 answers per card, says plainly that this is too few to call, and keeps the counts visible.
screens.instead: Too few to call: 7 people answered, but only 4 were counted on each belief and each needs 5, for this reason; get at least one more superintendent who fits counted on each belief before deciding anything about the solution.

screens.why_b1: "Too few to call" sits directly beside the number that decides it: 4 counted, 5 needed.
screens.why_b2: The 4 people counted and the for and against split are plain, but I had to look twice at the bar because "3 of 4" sits beside "no more than 1 in 3" and the strip has a fifth, empty cell.
screens.why_b3: The Compatibility name and the talk-over-the-noise belief are the ones I checked on the way in.
screens.why_b4: Asking Ray about his no is a real step, but the screen doesn't say that I need one more counted answer or what a no would mean for narrating videos on site.
screens.why_b5: It keeps n visible, says Luis's guess wasn't counted, calls this a small group and a lean, and says nothing is settled.
screens.instead: Too few to call: 3 of the 4 counted say they could talk over the noise, which leans your way, but you need one more counted answer, so firm up Luis's guess or ask another super, and ask Ray what stopped him, because if noise rules out narrating on site, the videos need another way in.

screens.why_b1: "Too few to call" is stated, and the deciding number sits with it and is repeated in the So line: 4 counted, 5 needed.
screens.why_b2: Better 3 and Same 1 over 4 people read at once, but I need a second look at the bar because it is given as both "3 of 4" and "no more than 1 in 3", and the fifth, uncounted cell has to be matched to Luis.
screens.why_b3: The name, Relative advantage, and the line about my last daily log and hours back at the end of the day are the ones I checked on the way in.
screens.why_b4: "Nothing is settled here yet" tells me not to act on this and implies I need one more counted answer, but it never says to get one or what this result means for Fresco.
screens.why_b5: It makes no claim beyond these people and says plainly that a small group is a lean, not a call, but the header's "4 answered" is a soft misstatement because 5 answered and 4 were counted.
screens.instead: Too few to call: 5 superintendents answered, 4 counted (Luis's was a guess), and 3 of the 4 said a lot better; it leans your way, but get one more counted answer before you trust hours back as the reason to buy.

screens.why_b1: "Too few to call" is at the top with the number that decides it beside it, 4 against the 5 needed, and the So line repeats both.
screens.why_b2: The answer counts and my bar at 3 of 4 are plain, but the header's "4 answered" clashes with the count line's "5 answered · 4 counted", so I need a second look to see that the base is the 4 counted and that Luis is the one left out.
screens.why_b3: The card is titled Adoption friction and its line, "Most would take short videos and talk over them on walks", is the belief I checked, word for word.
screens.why_b4: "Nothing is settled here yet" tells me not to act on it, but not that one more counted superintendent would allow a call, or that I should look at the two conditional yeses, since whether supers do this on walks decides whether the product works.
screens.why_b5: It claims nothing beyond these people: n is visible, the small group is called "a lean, not a call", the two conditional yeses are flagged, Luis's guess is left out by name, and the "4 answered" slip understates the responses rather than overstating the result.
screens.instead: Too few to call: 5 answered, but Luis's was a guess, so 4 counted and 5 are needed. So far 3 of 4 would do it, 2 of them only if it was clearly worth it; get one more superintendent's clear answer and find out what "worth it" means to those two before relying on videos on walks.

screens.why_b1: Each box opens on the verdict, "Too few to call", with the deciding number right beside it: 4 answered, 5 needed.
screens.why_b3: The dimension names and both belief lines are the ones I checked on the way in, including "talk over the noise on site" and "hours back at the end of the day".
screens.why_b4: "5 needed to call it" implies I need one more answer, but the screen never says that or what these two objections mean for the idea.
screens.why_b5: The low n is said on both lines, each theme is shown as one person with "1 against", and nothing is claimed beyond those who answered.
screens.why_b6: I did not type that a log can wait till morning when the schedule is slipping, or that a super who finishes it on a tablet before the gate loses the day to schedule and subs, so the hours may not be the pain; Ray's quote does not address noise, but it still adds to what I wrote.
screens.instead: Too few to call: 4 answered, 5 needed, so get at least one more answer on each line; so far, one super says the log waits when the schedule slips, and one already finishes it before leaving and loses the day to subs and schedule, so check whether hours back on the log is the benefit supers want.

screens.why1: It's the first thing asked and it makes sense to check straight off whether my jobs run on Procore or ACC before asking about my daily logs.
screens.why2: Procore and ACC are words I use every day, and "any job you run now" is how I'd say it, so I get it on the first read or hearing.
screens.why3: I know without thinking what platform each of my jobs is on.
screens.why4: Yes and No cover it because it's a plain fact about my jobs, and a screener needs no escape.
screens.why5: Nothing about a product or the founder's idea reaches me, only the software names my trade already uses.
screens.why6: It's short and ACC says fine as three letters, but "I'll read 2 options" is stiff before a plain yes or no, and the screener's form is the stem and then "Yes or no."
screens.instead: Is any job you run now on Procore or ACC? Yes or no.

screens.why1: After asking if my job is on Procore or ACC, it makes sense to ask whether I actually did the log work this week before asking for the story.
screens.why2: Site notes and daily log are my everyday words, and I can answer on first read whether I retyped them this week.
screens.why3: I do the daily log myself, so I know whether I retyped my notes in the last 5 working days, even though my bigger time sink is uploading photos.
screens.why4: Yes and No cover it, but the two chips don't fit: this asks about any log in five days rather than one particular log, and the guidelines allow no escape on a gate, so *I'd rather not say* shouldn't be there.
screens.why5: It asks only about my notes and the log, and nothing about a product, a company or the founder's terms reaches me.
screens.why6: Said aloud, it is one short question followed by *Yes or no*, with nothing to hold in my head and no second escape spoken, and I can answer after hearing it once.
screens.instead: In the last 5 working days, did you retype your site notes into the daily log? Yes / No (no chips)

screens.why1: I just said I retype my site notes into the daily log, and the kicker says here's an idea to consider, so a card about getting walk notes into Procore follows naturally.
screens.why2: I get all of it on first read and assignees is a Procore word, but scribe isn't a word anyone on my site would use; I'd say it writes up the notes.
screens.why3: I walk the site, take photos, chase the crew on action items and log in Procore every day, so I can picture exactly where this would fit in my day.
screens.why4: The card has no options, rows, chips or value box.
screens.why5: It's an idea card shown on purpose, plainly described, and no founder plans or terms for people like me reach me beyond the product itself.
screens.why6: It says fine in short sentences and I can follow it once, but the last line re-lists the videos, notes and Procore or ACC just said instead of pointing back to the how as §17 asks, so the end sounds like a repeat.
screens.instead: Imagine Fresco, notes from site walk videos. During the walk, you take short videos and talk over them. The AI writes them up as notes with photos, who it's assigned to and due dates, texts the crew their action items, and sends the notes to Procore or ACC in one click. The people building it believe this would get your walk into the log without the retyping.

screens.why1: Right after the idea card about notes from site walk videos, it makes sense to ask whether I could actually talk on site over the equipment noise.
screens.why2: Noise on site is my everyday world, but "talked over the noise" doesn't say to whom or into what, and "your last daily log" points me to the trailer when the noise is out on the walk, so I need a second read to get that it means narrating into the phone.
screens.why3: I walk the site every day and know exactly how loud it gets and whether I could talk through it during a pour or with saws and lifts running.
screens.why4: The four run cleanly from easily to no, they are in plain words, and "I can't tell" fits if I've never tried talking into a phone on a walk.
screens.why5: Nothing leaks beyond the idea card shown on purpose, and noise on site is my word, not a founder's term.
screens.why6: Heard once it is short, with one anchor, one question, four short options and one escape at the end, so I could answer straight away.
screens.instead: Think of your last site walk. Could you have talked into your phone over the noise on site? Yes, easily; yes, most of the time; only sometimes; or no. Or say you can't tell.

screens.why1: I've just been shown the idea and asked if I could have talked on site, so asking whether it would have helped my last daily log is the obvious next question.
screens.why2: Daily log is my everyday word and I get the question on first read, even if "go better" doesn't say whether it means faster or more accurate.
screens.why3: I know exactly how my last log went, but I've only got one line about turning site walk videos into notes and I shoot photos, so I'd be partly guessing how much it would help.
screens.why4: Better, no difference or worse covers my answer without overlap, the words are plain, and "I can't tell" fits something I've never used.
screens.why5: The card is shown on purpose and the question adds no company talk or role labels, just the product name and what it does.
screens.why6: It's one short question with four short options I can hold after hearing them once, and one escape at the end.

screens.why1: Right after asking if I could talk over the site noise and if it would have helped my log, it makes sense to ask if I'd actually do what the tool needs.
screens.why2: Short videos and talking over them on my walks are plain words, and I get it on the first read or hearing.
screens.why3: I walk the site every day with my phone and already take photos, so I know whether I'd shoot video and talk over it.
screens.why4: The four answers run cleanly from yes to no in words I'd use, my real answer of doing it when it paid off fits the second one, and I can't tell works as the escape.
screens.why5: The card shows the idea on purpose, and nothing beyond what I need to answer about the product or how the founder talks about people reaches me.
screens.why6: Said aloud, it's two short sentences with one question, and four short options plus the escape are easy to hold after one hearing.
